sources.title: Two-Pass Shock Propagation for Stable Stacking with Gauss-Seidel
Author reference implementation
sources.note: Read for algorithm interpretation only. No repository license file was present in the inspected tree; do not copy its code. Derive the experiment independently from Silk primitives and attribute the method.

hypothesis: Test stable gravity-directed ordering separately from a bounded withheld-impulse adaptation. Do not infer that either reproduces the reference implementation or its published speedups.
variants: two-pass with one sweep per layer per direction

stage_mapping.graph: Build once after contact refresh and normal constraint preparation; preserve the original prepared-row mapping and cache storage.
stage_mapping.biased: Ordering-only visits ascending graph layers. Two-pass solves ascending layers with lower-body response withheld, then visits descending layers, releasing accumulated responses to each layer before resolving its support constraints. Preserve source order inside each layer.
stage_mapping.relaxation_and_restitution: Unchanged scalar unbiased relaxation and final restitution; friction remains active inside each manifold solve.
stage_mapping.budget: Baseline and ordering-only use one biased manifold evaluation per substep; two-pass uses two. Report actual evaluations including failed attempts/fallback, rather than presenting equal substeps as equal work.

graph.vertices: Dynamic bodies in each existing island. Static bodies are support boundaries.
graph.edges: Orient contacts by body position projected against gravity, using double arithmetic. Equal projected heights are ambiguous and select the cycle/equal-height fallback.
graph.algorithm: Bounded adjacency arrays, indegrees and a lowest-slot-first heap for topological traversal; longest support distance defines a layer. Sort contact indices by layer then original row using nonrecursive heapsort.
fallbacks: unrooted dynamic body without a static-support path
graph.dynamic_policy: Unsupported free-flight components keep Soft Step. Supported toppling components are exercised rather than excluded by an unmeasured velocity cutoff.

scratch_budget.body_components: Four uint32 arrays (heads, indegrees, layers, queue) plus saved linear/angular velocities and deferred linear/angular responses (two groups of three floats).
scratch_budget.contact_components: Adjacency next and ordered-index arrays (8 bytes), plus a snapshot of the existing 144-byte prepared constraint for transactional fallback.
scratch_budget.ownership: Carve scratch and fixed context from the existing initialization-owned solver arena. No step allocation, recursion, public production selector, or permanent alternative backend.

finite_transaction: Snapshot the island velocities and prepared constraints before the two-pass attempt. Evaluate top-body responses and withheld lower-body responses in finite local state. If release or any complete candidate state is invalid, restore the snapshots and execute the original biased stage. Never retain a half-applied non-finite impulse.

fixtures.quality: Keep existing matrix thresholds. Pin new geometry and quality windows on the unoptimized baseline before comparing variants. Measure penetration, movement, residual speed, support/load transfer, momentum where external forces permit comparison, and failure/fallback coverage.

evidence: Five matched release runs, repeated same-binary determinism, actual graph/constraint work and exact memory. Validate sleep-disabled behavior and sleep-enabled compatibility separately. Run original physical/replay tests on experiments and record failures without loosening them.
decision_rule: Adopt only if physical and runtime evidence justify the change at the intended bounded budget. Otherwise retain Soft Step and archive only the reproducible experiment patch, harness and decision data; leave no runtime dispatch.
